title: ACH — Baseline
description: Array of baseline records. One element is one participant.
$comment: Not enforceable here: participant_id is unique across rows, one record per participant (S01:Variables row 2, D009).

allOf.$comment: Skip pattern R001: people who have not smoked 100 cigarettes (smk_ever = 2), or who refused or did not know (-7, -9), skip the smoking questions that follow, so smk_status, cigs_day and smk_age_start are -6. Questionnaire ¶8: 'IF NO, GO TO SECTION C.'; the data steward says refusals and don't-know answers at B1 were routed like No (D017) and confirms the -6 coding (D018); dictionary Codes row 2: -6 is 'Question not asked of this participant (skip pattern)'.

Applicability R001: people who have smoked 100 cigarettes (smk_ever = 1) were asked whether they smoke now and when they started, so smk_status and smk_age_start are never -6. Questionnaire ¶8 to ¶11: only 'No' at B1 skips B2 to B4 (refusals and don't-know answers count as No: D017); the data steward confirms the rule matches the delivered data (D018).

Skip pattern R002: former smokers (smk_status = 2), and people who did not know (-9) whether they smoke now, were not asked how many cigarettes they smoke, so cigs_day is -6. Questionnaire ¶10: 'IF SMOKES NOW:'; dictionary Variables row 11: 'Current smokers only'; a don't-know answer is treated like No (D017 for the first question, confirmed for this one in D029); the data steward confirms the -6 coding (D018).
Applicability R002: current smokers (smk_status = 1) were asked how many cigarettes they smoke, so cigs_day is never -6. The data steward confirms the rule matches the delivered data (D018).

Skip pattern R003: men (sex = 1), and people whose sex was refused (-7), skip the women's-health section, so menarche_age, parity, age_first_birth and breastfed_ever are -6. Questionnaire ¶13: 'ASK SECTION C OF WOMEN ONLY (A2 = 2). MEN: GO TO SECTION D.'; dictionary Variables rows 13 and 14: 'Women only'; the data steward says a refused sex is skipped like men (D021) and confirms the -6 coding (D022).

Applicability R003: women (sex = 2) were asked the age at first period and the number of live births, so menarche_age and parity are never -6. The data steward confirms the rule matches the delivered data (D022).

Skip pattern R004: people who were not told they have diabetes (diabetes_dx = 2), or who did not know (-9), were not asked the age at diagnosis, so diabetes_age is -6. Questionnaire ¶21: 'IF YES:'; dictionary Variables row 19: 'Asked only if diabetes_dx = 1'; the data steward says a don't-know answer means the age was not asked (D024) and confirms the -6 coding (D025).

Applicability R004: people who were told they have diabetes (diabetes_dx = 1) were asked the age at diagnosis, so diabetes_age is never -6. The data steward confirms the rule matches the delivered data (D025).

Skip pattern R005: women with no live births (parity = 0) have no first birth and no children to breastfeed, so age_first_birth and breastfed_ever are -6. The documents do not state this routing; the data steward vouches for it (D020).

Applicability R005: women with at least one live birth (parity 1 to 15) were asked the age at first birth and about breastfeeding, so age_first_birth and breastfed_ever are never -6 (they may still be refused or don't know). The documents do not state this routing; the data steward vouches for it (D020).
